newsitem.title: USA: Republican Senator floats end to U.S. gains tax.
newsitem.headline: Republican Senator floats end to U.S. gains tax.

text.p: Senate Republican Whip Don Nickles on Tuesday floated a proposal to end the separate tax on capital gains as one issue that should be considered when Congress debates tax cuts this year.

Nickles, of Oklahoma, told reporters that the idea he was considering would leave gains on investments untaxed so long as they were rolled over into new investments. And, if the investment were liquidated, the profits would be considered ordinary income.
Nickles is a member of the Senate Finance Committee which is to consider Republican and Democratic plans to reduce taxes.
The Republican capital gains tax cut would be effective Jan. 1, 1997.
"We need to reduce the tax on transactions," Nickles said later on the Senate floor.

Nickles provided details on another key element of the Republican tax plan providing a $500 per child tax credit up to age 18. It would begin to be phased out at incomes of $75,000 for an individual and $110,000 for a couple and would not be refundable, meaning it would not give federal payments to very low income families.
The entire tax package, which also includes estate tax relief, retirement savings incentives, and tax deductions for losses on home sales, is worth some $170 billion over five years.
Separately, Sen. Richard Lugar, R-Indiana, proposed a single rate consumption tax be substituted for the current income and estate tax system.
